title: Jonah and the Tide
premise: Silas Thornbury has built her career on erasure: as a celebrated ghostwriter, she pens other people's truths while burying her own, including the anonymous letters she wrote for ten years to a stranger she loved and lost. When that stranger, maritime historian Elias Vane, moves in next door weeks before the coastal town's Lantern Festival, she realizes he never knew his beloved correspondent was her—and worse, he's publishing a memoir she's been secretly hired to ghostwrite under a rival's name. As festival preparations force them together, Silas must decide whether to keep profiting from stolen voices or claim her own, knowing exposure could destroy both their careers. In the end, she confesses everything at the festival's lantern release, loses the contract but gains something rarer: a life where she is finally seen.
about_author: Marguerite Pemberton is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who spent fifteen years writing other people's stories before claiming one of her own. She lives on the Atlantic coast, where she collects tide charts and answers letters slowly, on purpose.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Silas finishes ghostwriting a celebrity chef's memoir, invisible at her own book launch. POV: Silas. Establishes her talent, her self-erasure, and the ache of writing intimacy she doesn't live. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as professional pride.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Silas recalls the decade of letters she exchanged with a stranger met through a misdirected postcard—letters that ended abruptly three years ago. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: tender grief for a love that existed only on paper.

chapters.title: The Moving Van Next Door
chapters.summary: A new neighbor arrives in her coastal town: Elias Vane, the letter-writer himself, older and guarded. He doesn't recognize her; they'd only ever traded words. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: shock curdling into fear of discovery.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Silas accepts a lucrative, secretive contract: ghostwriting a rival author's memoir about a famous shipwreck rescue—a story Elias has researched his whole life. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: complicity; she feels power's corrupting pull and takes the money anyway.

chapters.title: Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Elias asks Silas to help with the town's Lantern Festival archives; proximity forces small talk, then real conversation. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: cautious warmth, each hiding a secret from the other.

chapters.title: What the Rival Knew
chapters.summary: Silas discovers her client, Vivian Marsh, fabricated key details of the rescue memoir to discredit Elias's scholarship. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—her words will become someone else's weapon.

chapters.title: Interviews with a Stranger
chapters.summary: Under pretext of 'local color,' Silas interviews Elias for the memoir, harvesting his life's work while he confides about the letters he still keeps in a tin box. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: bittersweet confession to the wrong audience.

chapters.title: The Tin Box
chapters.summary: Elias shows Silas one letter; she recognizes her own handwriting disguised by old habits. She nearly confesses, then flees. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror of being known versus longing for it.

chapters.title: Vivian's Terms
chapters.summary: Vivian tightens the contract: Silas must sign away credit permanently and deliver the manuscript before the festival. A veiled threat reminds Silas how much she owes her career to silence. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: claustrophobic entrapment.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Confessions Half-Made
chapters.summary: A storm strands Silas and Elias in the archive; he describes the letter-writer so precisely that Silas almost believes he'd forgive her. Almost-kiss interrupted. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: hope rising against judgment.

chapters.title: Draft One of Someone Else's Truth
chapters.summary: Silas writes the fraudulent rescue chapter brilliantly and hates herself for it. Her editor praises the 'voice.' POV: Silas. Emotional beat: corruption completing itself; craft without conscience feels like drowning.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Festival planning throws them together publicly; the town assumes a romance. Vivian arrives early, watching. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: performance versus authenticity; stakes tighten.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Elias tells Silas he turned down a prestigious post to stay in this town—the first place he belonged. Silas realizes she's never belonged anywhere but inside others' books. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: mirror held up to her invisibility.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Working late, Silas secretly drafts a true version of the rescue story in her own voice—just for herself. It's the best thing she's ever written. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reclamation stirring.

chapters.title: Vivian Finds Out
chapters.summary: Vivian discovers Silas's connection to Elias and threatens to expose her as both ghostwriter and letter-writer unless the false memoir ships untouched. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: blackmail; the trap snaps shut.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Sent
chapters.summary: Silas writes Elias a full confession and can't deliver it. Instead she asks him, obliquely, whether truth matters more than the person carrying it. His answer wounds her. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: despair; justice seems impossible inside the law of contracts.

chapters.title: Breaking the Contract
chapters.summary: Silas confronts Vivian, refusing to sign the final page, forfeiting the fee that pays her debts. Vivian promises ruin. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: costly defiance; choosing integrity over survival.

chapters.title: Everything Undone
chapters.summary: Vivian publishes excerpts anyway, exposing Silas's ghostwriting and twisting the letters into scandal. Elias learns the truth from a headline, not from her. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: betrayal; the darkest hour.

chapters.title: Lantern Night
chapters.summary: At the festival's lantern release, before the whole town, Silas reads aloud her true account of the rescue and her true identity as the letter-writer—claiming every word as hers. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax; visibility as sacrifice and liberation.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The town, moved, rallies: archivists verify Silas's honest version, Vivian's fraud collapses publicly, and no lawsuit can touch a story told freely. Elias says nothing yet. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by uncertainty.

chapters.title: The Reply
chapters.summary: Days later, a letter appears under Silas's door—in Elias's handwriting, answering her decade-old final letter point by point, ending with an invitation to write back in person. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered, not demanded.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Tide
chapters.summary: One year later: Silas publishes her first book under her own name at the festival; Elias stands beside her, no longer reader or rival but partner. She signs the title page herself. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the tide returns what it took.
